A hoist is a mechanical lift or hydraulic

attached to a ceiling

moving

paralyzed, tetraplegia)

text:
B. Patient postural preparation (Wheelchair to bed)
Starting from the seats
1. Place the wheelchair/training chair and bed in the
appropriate position so that there is enough space
to operate the repositioner, and also lock the
wheelchair/bed wheels.
2. Release the patient's safety belt/restraints, assist
the patient in leaning forward, pull the sling bag
down as much as possible to wrap the patient's head
and body propulsion, then help the patient lean back
in the chair.
3. Wear the sling on both sides of the thighs, and
wrap the patient's thighs from the outside in,
bottom to top. It is necessary to pull the sling strap
upward as much as possible to reduce the space at
the bottom of the sling sling for the patient's hip.

text:
B. Patient postural preparation(Bed to W/C)
1. Place the bed and wheelchair/training chair in
appropriate positions so that there is enough space
to operate the transfer machine, and also lock the
wheelchair/bed wheels.
2. Raise the bed to the appropriate height and
unfasten the patient's restraints.
3. Assist the patient in turning to one side, then fold
half of the sling from the other side to the
patient's body. Then help the patient turn to the
other side and pull out the other half of the sling to
return the patient to a flat position.
4. Wear the sling on both sides of the thighs, and
wrap the patient's thighs from the outside in,
bottom to top. It is necessary to pull the sling strap
upward as much as possible to reduce the space at
the bottom of the sling sling for the patient's hip.
